case_title: Satpal Singh v. The State of Punjab
statutory_provisions: NDPS Act s. 37; Cr.P.C. ss. 438 and 439
neutral_facts: The accused, along with two co-accused, were involved in a case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act. The police registered an FIR against them for offenses punishable under Sections 22 and 29 of the NDPS Act. The High Court initially granted anticipatory bail to the co-accused but later rejected the application, noting that the order did not take into account Section 37 of the NDPS Act, which imposes stringent limitations on granting bail for offenses involving commercial quantities. The Sessions Court released the accused on regular bail based on an interim order from the High Court, but the Supreme Court set aside this order, stating that the High Court's order did not properly consider the requirements of Section 37. The accused were directed to surrender before the trial court, with the option to apply for regular bail if they so desired.
